a: A tiled layer whose one axis is empty still walks every copy index of the other, so a negative bleed can spin the draw for up to 2^53 iterations
`plane.set({ pan: undefined })` is accepted and makes every later draw of the plane throw
b: A bare-number `bleed` widens only the x axis, so a lattice tiled on both axes pops content in at its top and bottom edges
`plane.set({ pan: undefined })` makes every later draw of the parallax layer throw
A y range emptied by a negative bleed lets the copy-count guard pass, and the x loop then runs once per column with nothing to draw
